category_title: Students with 'loud' classroom presence who leverage personal stories for health advocacy
scenario_title: Connecting everyday stories to science topics in group discussions
minimal_context: The student is participating in a Lunchtime Science group discussion and reviewing a case study about prenatal health and the environment.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Please read this case study about prenatal health and the environment and share your thoughts with the group.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Speaking loudly over the group) Why do we have to talk about this? I'm not wanting to be a mom, so this has nothing to do with me.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's just focus on the reading. What do you think about the article?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I mean, I was at the store yesterday and my friend was yelling about these new shoes she bought. It was crazy.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Can you try to connect that story to the science topic we are discussing?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I don't know how it connects. Like I said, my friends and I are not nature people. This whole science thing just doesn't give me any new material or ways to interact with people.

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: Please read this case study about prenatal health and the environment and share your thoughts with the group.

STUDENT: (Speaking loudly over the group) Why do we have to talk about this? I'm not wanting to be a mom, so this has nothing to do with me.

TUTOR: Let's just focus on the reading. What do you think about the article?

STUDENT: I mean, I was at the store yesterday and my friend was yelling about these new shoes she bought. It was crazy.

TUTOR: Can you try to connect that story to the science topic we are discussing?

STUDENT: I don't know how it connects. Like I said, my friends and I are not nature people. This whole science thing just doesn't give me any new material or ways to interact with people.

task.content: Reflecting on the relevance of Lunchtime Science topics (prenatal health and environment) to their personal identities and participating in group discussions.
task.learning_goal: Construct a scientific story rooted in personal narratives and act as a knowledge authority.

context.materials: Newspaper articles, case studies of hypothetical friends, resources about chemicals in cigarettes
context.social_setting: Group discussions with peers and instructors from different racial backgrounds

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: When attempting to share everyday stories during group discussions
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Shared everyday stories where it was difficult to infer how they were relevant to the conversation. Were less likely to participate in LS despite having a 'loud' presence in the classroom.
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: Felt marginalized by school; felt LS did not provide new material or new possible images for ways of interacting with others.
related_quotes: not taken up on the social plane

behavior_patterns.condition: When reflecting on the relevance of topics like prenatal health and environment
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Described themselves as 'not nature people' and 'not wanting to be a mom', showing resistance to the topics.
behavior_patterns.internal_state: Historical narratives countered activities in LS
related_quotes: not wanting to be a mom
